headline: Italian drugmaker Italfarmaco and AI company VeriSIM Life have started a drug-discovery partnership with a potential value above $100 million.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an early-stage drug-discovery deal with a large potential value but no named candidate.
importance_line: People with neuromuscular, fibrotic and other rare diseases are the eventual targets, but with no drug candidate named and no upfront terms disclosed this is an early commitment rather than a treatment, and the $100 million is a potential total, not money paid.
summary: AllSci reports that Italfarmaco, an Italian drugmaker, and VeriSIM Life, a San Francisco company that uses AI to design drugs, will work to develop drugs that block an undisclosed HDAC target (a member of an enzyme family that helps control gene activity) for neuromuscular, fibrotic (tissue-scarring) and rare diseases. AllSci puts the deal's total potential value above $100 million, with VeriSIM eligible for service fees, milestone payments and royalties, and says the upfront terms were not disclosed and no drug candidate or clinical program has been named.
notes: Business Wire release (the pool's link) returned HTTP 000 and the companies' sites had no copy; read AllSci's own report of the same announcement and credit it.
